title: Connectors: Weil, Denn, and Dass
summary: Master the essential A2 sentence connectors: understand the crucial grammatical difference between weil (subordinating: conjugated verb moves to the end) and denn (coordinating: verb stays in position 2). Master dass-clauses for reporting thoughts and describing graphs, handle modal verbs, separable verbs, and the perfect tense in subordinate clauses, and use inverted word order when the subordinate clause comes first.
definition: Connectors (Konnektoren / Konjunktionen) link words, phrases, or clauses to build longer, more expressive sentences. Chapter 4 focuses on giving reasons with weil and denn, and reporting statements, thoughts, or observations with dass.

definition_examples.german: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland lebe.
definition_examples.english: I learn German because I live in Germany. (Subordinate clause: verb 'lebe' at the very end!)

definition_examples.german: Ich lerne Deutsch, denn ich lebe in Deutschland.
definition_examples.english: I learn German, and the reason is that I live in Germany. (Main clause: verb 'lebe' stays in position 2!)

definition_examples.german: Wir wissen, dass sie bei Siemens arbeitet.
definition_examples.english: We know that she works at Siemens. (Subordinate clause: verb 'arbeitet' at the very end!)

rows: **Nebensatz:** Conjugated verb moves to the **very end**
Ich gehe ins Bett, **weil ich müde bin**.
because / and the reason is that
Ich gehe ins Bett, **denn ich bin müde**.
**Nebensatz:** Conjugated verb moves to the **very end**
Er hat gesagt, **dass er krank ist**.
Es ist kalt, **aber die Sonne scheint**.

rules: **1. The Meaning vs. Position Rule:** A connector's meaning tells you how two ideas connect (reason, contrast, report); the connector's grammatical type dictates where the conjugated verb must stand.
**2. The 'weil' Rule (Verb-Final):** *weil* introduces a subordinate clause (*Nebensatz*). The conjugated verb that is usually in position 2 moves to the very end: *..., weil ich krank bin*.

**3. The 'denn' Rule (Position 2 Unchanged):** *denn* connects two independent main clauses (*Hauptsätze*). It counts as Position 0; the subject takes Position 1 and the conjugated verb stays in Position 2: *..., denn ich bin krank*.

**4. The 'dass' Rule (Verb-Final):** *dass* (that) introduces a subordinate clause reporting what someone says, thinks, knows, believes, or feels. The conjugated verb moves to the very end: *Ich weiß, dass du recht hast*.
**5. Always Use a Comma:** In German, you must always place a comma before *weil*, *denn*, and *dass* when linking clauses.

**6. Inversion when Nebensatz comes first:** If the *weil*-clause or *dass*-clause comes first, the following main clause begins immediately with its conjugated verb: *Weil ich müde bin, gehe ich ins Bett*.
**7. Modal Verbs at Clause End:** The infinitive stands first, and the conjugated modal verb goes to the very end: *..., weil ich früh aufstehen muss*.

**8. Separable Verbs at Clause End:** In a subordinate clause (*weil* / *dass*), separable prefixes do NOT separate; they are written together as a single word at the end: *..., weil ich früh aufstehe*.
**9. Perfect Tense at Clause End:** The past participle (*Partizip II*) comes before the conjugated auxiliary (*haben/sein*): *..., weil er gestern gearbeitet hat*.

usage_rules.title: Forming Reason Clauses with 'weil' (Step-by-Step)
usage_rules.rule: Take two independent statements, insert a comma and 'weil', and send the conjugated verb of the second sentence to the very end.
usage_rules.note: Sentence 1: 'Ich lerne Deutsch.' + Sentence 2: 'Ich lebe in Deutschland.' → 'Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland lebe.'

examples.de: Er geht ins Bett, weil er müde ist.
examples.en: He is going to bed because he is tired. (ist moves to the end)

examples.de: Ich komme heute nicht, weil ich krank bin.
examples.en: I am not coming today because I am ill. (bin moves to the end)

examples.de: Warum studierst du Mathematik? — Ich studiere Mathematik, weil ich sie interessant finde.
examples.en: Why are you studying mathematics? — I study mathematics because I find it interesting.

usage_rules.title: 'weil' vs. 'denn' (The Golden Word Order Contrast)
usage_rules.rule: Both words translate to 'because'. Use 'weil' for everyday spoken German (verb kicked to end). Use 'denn' in writing and exams to vary your sentences without altering main-clause word order.
usage_rules.note: Compare: '..., weil ich müde bin' (Verb at end) vs. '..., denn ich bin müde' (Verb in Pos. 2).

examples.de: Ich gehe früh ins Bett, weil ich morgen früh aufstehen muss.
examples.en: I go to bed early because I must get up early tomorrow.

examples.de: Ich gehe früh ins Bett, denn ich muss morgen früh aufstehen.
examples.en: I go to bed early, and the reason is that I must get up early tomorrow.

usage_rules.title: Using 'dass' to Report Thoughts, Knowledge, and Graphs
usage_rules.rule: 'dass' (that) introduces the content of what someone says, thinks, believes, knows, hopes, or feels. It also introduces descriptions of statistics, graphs, and charts in A2/B1 exam tasks.
usage_rules.note: Useful chart starters: 'Die Grafik zeigt, dass ...' / 'Man kann sehen, dass ...'

examples.de: Er hat gesagt, dass er krank ist.
examples.en: He said that he is ill.

examples.de: Ich denke, dass er nicht kommen wird.
examples.en: I think that he will not come.

examples.de: Die Grafik zeigt, dass Kinder das Handy zwei Stunden pro Tag nutzen.
examples.en: The graph shows that children use mobile phones for two hours per day.

examples.de: Man kann sehen, dass Studierende das Handy am meisten nutzen.
examples.en: One can see that university students use mobile phones the most.

usage_rules.title: Complex Verb Forms in Subordinate Clauses (Modal, Separable, Perfekt)
usage_rules.rule: In subordinate clauses (weil / dass), the verb bracket changes: 1) Modal verbs: Infinitive + Modal (*aufstehen muss*). 2) Separable verbs: Joined together into one word (*anruft*, *aufstehe*). 3) Perfect tense: Participle + Auxiliary (*gearbeitet hat*, *geöffnet hast*).
usage_rules.note: The conjugated part ALWAYS goes to the very end of the clause!

examples.de: Ich denke, dass ich heute nicht arbeiten kann.
examples.en: I think that I cannot work today.

examples.de: Ich hoffe, dass sie mich morgen anruft.
examples.en: I hope that she calls me tomorrow.

examples.de: Thomas hat heute frei, weil er gestern gearbeitet hat.
examples.en: Thomas has today off because he worked yesterday.

sections.heading: 4.1 What Are Connectors? (Was sind Konnektoren?)
sections.core_difference: Connectors (Konnektoren / Konjunktionen) link words, phrases, or complete clauses. Without connectors, speech sounds robotic and disjointed ('I am tired. I go to bed.'). With connectors, ideas flow naturally ('I am going to bed because I am tired'). In A2, connectors are critical for writing letters and conversational fluency.

comparison.meaning: Connectors that link two independent main clauses without changing word order.
comparison.how_to_identify: Position 0 connectors: und (and), aber (but), oder (or), denn (because), sondern (rather).
comparison.example: Es ist kalt, aber die Sonne scheint.
comparison.english: It is cold, but the sun is shining.
comparison.trick: Think: ADUSO connectors do not touch the verb position (verb stays in Pos. 2)!

comparison.meaning: Connectors that introduce a dependent clause and kick the conjugated verb to the end.
comparison.example: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil es kalt ist.
comparison.english: I am staying at home because it is cold.
comparison.trick: Think: Subordinating connectors kick the verb to the very end of the sentence!

rows: because / and the reason is that

sections.rule_of_thumb: Always learn two things about every new connector: 1) What it means, and 2) Where it puts the conjugated verb!

sections.heading: 4.2 Weil — Giving a Reason (Subordinate Clause)
sections.core_difference: 'weil' introduces a subordinate clause (Nebensatz) that explains the reason or cause for an action. It answers the question 'Warum?' (Why?). In a weil-clause, the conjugated verb is pushed to the very end, and a comma must precede 'weil'.

patterns.pattern: Standard Order: Hauptsatz + , weil + Subject + ... + Verb am Ende
patterns.example: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland lebe.
patterns.meaning: Main clause (verb in Pos. 2) followed by comma and weil-clause (verb 'lebe' at end).

patterns.pattern: Inverted Order: Weil-Clause first + , Verb + Subject + ...
patterns.example: Weil ich in Deutschland lebe, lerne ich Deutsch.
patterns.meaning: The entire weil-clause occupies Position 1; the main clause starts immediately with its verb 'lerne' in Position 2!

patterns.example: Warum studierst du Mathematik? — Weil ich sie interessant finde.
patterns.meaning: In casual conversation, the weil-clause can stand alone as a direct answer.

rows: Ich komme nicht. Ich bin krank.
Ich komme nicht, **weil ich krank bin**.
Conjugated verb *bin* moves to the end.
Ich gehe ins Bett. Ich muss früh aufstehen.
Ich gehe ins Bett, **weil ich früh aufstehen muss**.
Ich gehe ins Bett. Ich stehe früh auf.
Ich gehe ins Bett, **weil ich früh aufstehe**.
Prefix and stem reunite into one word: *aufstehe*.
Thomas hat frei. Er hat gestern gearbeitet.
Thomas hat frei, **weil er gestern gearbeitet hat**.

worked_example.german: Weil er gestern viel gearbeitet hat, schläft Thomas heute lange.
worked_example.english: Because he worked a lot yesterday, Thomas is sleeping late today.
worked_example.analysis: 1) The weil-clause comes first: auxiliary 'hat' is at the end of the subordinate clause. 2) After the comma, the main clause begins directly with the conjugated verb 'schläft' (Position 2), followed by the subject 'Thomas'.

sections.topic: 4.3 Denn — Giving a Reason with Main-Clause Word Order
sections.heading: 4.3 Denn — Giving a Reason with Main-Clause Word Order
sections.core_difference: 'denn' also means 'because' (literally: 'and the reason is that'). However, unlike 'weil', 'denn' is a coordinating conjunction. It links two main clauses and DOES NOT change the word order! The verb stays in Position 2.

comparison.example: Er geht ins Bett, denn er ist müde.
comparison.english: He goes to bed, and the reason is that he is tired.
comparison.trick: Do not move 'ist' to the end after denn!

comparison.what: Modal verb stays in Position 2; infinitive stays at the end.
comparison.example: Ich gehe früh ins Bett, denn ich muss morgen früh aufstehen.
comparison.english: I go to bed early, for I must get up early tomorrow.
comparison.trick: Word order is identical to a standard independent sentence.

comparison.what: Stem stays in Position 2; prefix stays at the end.
comparison.example: Ich gehe früh ins Bett, denn ich stehe morgen früh auf.
comparison.english: I go to bed early, for I get up early tomorrow.

comparison.what: Auxiliary stays in Position 2; Partizip II stays at the end.
comparison.example: Thomas hat heute frei, denn er hat gestern gearbeitet.
comparison.english: Thomas has the day off today, for he worked yesterday.
comparison.trick: Auxiliary 'hat' is in Position 2, 'gearbeitet' is at the end.

sections.rule_of_thumb: Stylistic Advice: In daily conversational speech, 'weil' is the standard choice. 'denn' is slightly more formal and elegant; use it in writing or exams when you want to avoid repeating 'weil' too many times.

sections.topic: 4.4 Dass — Reporting Statements, Thoughts, Feelings & Graphs
sections.heading: 4.4 Dass — Reporting Statements, Thoughts, Feelings & Graphs
sections.core_difference: 'dass' (that) introduces subordinate clauses that explain the content of what someone says, thinks, believes, knows, hopes, or feels. Like 'weil', 'dass' kicks the conjugated verb to the very end of the clause.

rows: Er hat gesagt, **dass er krank ist**.
Ich denke, **dass er nicht kommen wird**.
Wir wissen, **dass sie bei Siemens arbeitet**.
Ich hoffe, **dass sie mich morgen anruft**.
Ich mag es nicht, **dass du rauchst**.
Es ist wichtig, **dass du Mathematik lernst**.

same_sentence.german: Die Grafik zeigt, dass Kinder das Handy zwei Stunden pro Tag nutzen.
same_sentence.english: The graph shows that children use mobile phones for two hours per day.
same_sentence.analysis: A vital A2/B1 exam formula: 1) 'Die Grafik zeigt' (main clause) + 2) comma + 3) 'dass' + 4) Subject 'Kinder' + 5) Object/details 'das Handy zwei Stunden pro Tag' + 6) Conjugated verb 'nutzen' at the very end!

sections.trick: Exam Presentation Formula: Whenever you must describe a picture, statistic, or diagram in an exam, use: 'Die Grafik zeigt, dass ...' or 'Man kann sehen, dass ...' with the verb at the very end!

sections.topic: 4.5 Direct Comparison: weil vs. denn vs. dass
sections.heading: 4.5 Direct Comparison: weil vs. denn vs. dass
sections.core_difference: Look at these three connectors side-by-side to understand exactly how their meaning and verb position differ.

quick_comparison.german: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
quick_comparison.english: I am staying at home because I am ill.
quick_comparison.why: Gives a reason (why). 'weil' is subordinating → verb 'bin' at the end.

quick_comparison.german: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.
quick_comparison.english: I am staying at home, for I am ill.
quick_comparison.why: Gives a reason (why). 'denn' is coordinating → verb 'bin' in Position 2.

quick_comparison.german: Ich weiß, dass ich krank bin.
quick_comparison.english: I know that I am ill.
quick_comparison.why: Gives content (what I know). 'dass' is subordinating → verb 'bin' at the end.

quick_comparison.german: Er sagt, dass er müde ist, weil er viel gearbeitet hat.
quick_comparison.english: He says that he is tired because he worked a lot.
quick_comparison.why: Two subordinate clauses combined: 'dass' gives what he says, 'weil' gives why he is tired.

sections.rule_of_thumb: Summary Checklist: 1) Is it a reason? Use 'weil' (verb at end) or 'denn' (verb in Pos. 2). 2) Is it reporting a statement or fact? Use 'dass' (verb at end). 3) Always put a comma before all three!

commonMistakes.incorrect: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich lebe in Deutschland.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland lebe.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'weil' is a subordinating conjunction. The conjugated verb 'lebe' must be moved to the very end of the clause.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Ich lerne Deutsch, denn ich in Deutschland lebe.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich lerne Deutsch, denn ich lebe in Deutschland.
commonMistakes.explanation: 'denn' is a coordinating conjunction. The verb stays in Position 2; it does NOT move to the end.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Weil ich krank bin ich komme nicht.
commonMistakes.correct: Weil ich krank bin, komme ich nicht.
commonMistakes.explanation: When the subordinate clause comes first, the following main clause must begin immediately with the conjugated verb ('komme ich') after the comma.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Ich hoffe, dass sie mich anruft morgen.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich hoffe, dass sie mich morgen anruft.
commonMistakes.explanation: In a dass-clause, the verb (including separable verbs written together as 'anruft') must stand at the very end of the clause.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Ich gehe ins Bett weil ich müde bin.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich gehe ins Bett, weil ich müde bin.
commonMistakes.explanation: German strictly requires a comma before 'weil', 'denn', and 'dass'.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Ich denke, dass ich kann heute nicht arbeiten.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich denke, dass ich heute nicht arbeiten kann.
commonMistakes.explanation: With modal verbs in subordinate clauses, the infinitive comes first ('arbeiten') and the conjugated modal verb stands at the very end ('kann').

exercises.prompt: Ich bleibe im Bett, weil ich krank _______ . (sein)
exercises.hint: 'weil' kicks the conjugated verb to the very end: ich bin → 'weil ich krank bin'.

exercises.prompt: Ich bleibe im Bett, denn ich _______ krank. (sein)
exercises.hint: 'denn' connects main clauses; the verb stays in Position 2: 'denn ich bin krank'.

exercises.prompt: Er hat gesagt, dass er heute keine Zeit _______ . (haben)
exercises.hint: 'dass' kicks the conjugated verb to the very end: 'dass er heute keine Zeit hat'.

exercises.prompt: Weil ich müde bin, _______ ich ins Bett. (gehen)
exercises.hint: When the weil-clause comes first, the following main clause begins immediately with its conjugated verb: 'komme/gehe ich'.

exercises.prompt: Ich gehe früh schlafen, weil ich morgen früh aufstehen _______ . (müssen)
exercises.hint: With a modal verb in a subordinate clause, the modal verb goes to the very end after the infinitive: 'aufstehen muss'.

exercises.prompt: Ich hoffe, dass du mich morgen _______ . (anrufen)
exercises.hint: In a dass-clause, separable verbs are reunited into one word at the end: 'anrufst'.

exercises.prompt: Thomas hat heute frei, weil er gestern gearbeitet _______ . (haben)
exercises.hint: In the perfect tense, the auxiliary verb goes to the very end after the participle: 'gearbeitet hat'.

exercises.prompt: Die Grafik zeigt, dass viele Menschen Sport _______ . (treiben)
exercises.hint: In graph descriptions with 'dass', the conjugated verb 'treiben' stands at the very end.

exercises.prompt: Welcher Konnektor verändert die Verbposition NICHT? (weil / denn / dass)
exercises.hint: 'denn' is a coordinating conjunction (ADUSO) and leaves the verb in Position 2.

exercises.prompt: Muss vor 'weil', 'denn' und 'dass' ein Komma stehen? (ja / nein)
exercises.hint: In German grammar, a comma is strictly required before weil, denn, and dass.

mastery_goals: Fluently give reasons using both 'weil' (verb at end) and 'denn' (verb in position 2).
Correctly construct 'dass'-clauses for opinions, reported speech, and chart descriptions.
Correctly order modal verbs, separable verbs, and perfect tense in subordinate clauses.
Apply inverted word order when the subordinate clause comes first (Weil ..., gehe ich ...).
Categorize German connectors into subordinating (verb-final) and coordinating (position 2).
study_strategy: 1. Practice the Verb-Kick: When you say 'weil' or 'dass', pause and consciously send the verb to the end of the clause.
2. Pair 'weil' and 'denn': Write sentence pairs: 'Ich lerne, weil ich will' vs. 'Ich lerne, denn ich will'.
3. Practice chart sentences: Drill 'Die Grafik zeigt, dass ...' for your German exam speaking and writing modules.
4. Test yourself on the 10 self-check exercises below until you score 10/10.
